elements.name: GROUND-WEST · joist 017
elements.status: Experimental solid-timber candidate; limited floor-load screen only
elements.basis: Short northern suspended ground-floor bays use 45 × 295 mm solid C24 at 400 mm centres. This uses about 43% less net timber than the earlier 95 × 245 mm option; both are compared in G02. Garage vehicle bays remain the separate G01 concrete-deck concept. Same FFL, ceiling datum and support network; joists are 5 mm shallower than the earlier 300 mm I-joist reservation. Experimental floor-load candidate; no complete floor-system approval.
checks: Engineer to verify loading, capacity, stability and complete support path.
Coordinate bearings, connections, fire protection and installation tolerances before construction.

supportScreen.basis: G02: 45 × 295 mm C24 at 400 mm centres; 0.8225 m conservative receiver-centre span. Single simply supported joist, intact ends, no composite action or load sharing.
supportScreen.loadBasis: Assumed superimposed floor Gk 0.75 / 1.00 / 1.35 kPa, including a lightweight-partition allowance, plus joist self-weight at 4.2 kN/m³. Alternative Qk 1.50 / 1.50 / 2.00 kPa or one 2.00 kN midspan point on a single joist. The point and distributed cases are separate sensitivities, not simultaneous. Heavy walls, vehicles and plant are excluded from these timber bays. These are assumptions, not certified statutory bounds.
supportScreen.limits: Limited C24 bending, shear and deformation screen: Emean 11000 / Gmean 690 N/mm²; SC1; kdef 0.6; psi2 0.3; gammaM 1.3; kcr 0.67; kh=ksys=1. Instant <= min(L/300,8 mm), final <= min(L/250,10 mm) are study targets. Vibration, restraint, floor diaphragm, service penetrations, bearing and compatible hanger/ledger fixings, fire/acoustic/moisture assemblies and the onward load route remain unverified. No construction approval.

checks: Engineer to verify loading, capacity, stability and complete support path.

supportScreen.basis: G02: 45 × 295 mm C24 at 400 mm centres; 3.8725 m conservative receiver-centre span. Single simply supported joist, intact ends, no composite action or load sharing.

elements.name: GROUND-EAST · joist 025
elements.status: Experimental solid-timber candidate; limited floor-load screen only
elements.basis: Short northern suspended ground-floor bays use 45 × 295 mm solid C24 at 400 mm centres. This uses about 43% less net timber than the earlier 95 × 245 mm option; both are compared in G02. Garage vehicle bays remain the separate G01 concrete-deck concept. Same FFL, ceiling datum and support network; joists are 5 mm shallower than the earlier 300 mm I-joist reservation. Experimental floor-load candidate; no complete floor-system approval.
checks: Engineer to verify loading, capacity, stability and complete support path.
Coordinate bearings, connections, fire protection and installation tolerances before construction.

supportScreen.basis: G02: 45 × 295 mm C24 at 400 mm centres; 4.3825 m conservative receiver-centre span. Single simply supported joist, intact ends, no composite action or load sharing.
supportScreen.loadBasis: Assumed superimposed floor Gk 0.75 / 1.00 / 1.35 kPa, including a lightweight-partition allowance, plus joist self-weight at 4.2 kN/m³. Alternative Qk 1.50 / 1.50 / 2.00 kPa or one 2.00 kN midspan point on a single joist. The point and distributed cases are separate sensitivities, not simultaneous. Heavy walls, vehicles and plant are excluded from these timber bays. These are assumptions, not certified statutory bounds.
supportScreen.limits: Limited C24 bending, shear and deformation screen: Emean 11000 / Gmean 690 N/mm²; SC1; kdef 0.6; psi2 0.3; gammaM 1.3; kcr 0.67; kh=ksys=1. Instant <= min(L/300,8 mm), final <= min(L/250,10 mm) are study targets. No construction approval.

beamTopBearing.name: Gallery west upper pier · bearing bed above cross-beam
beamTopBearing.basis: Ten mm top bearing-bed envelope closes the finite beam pocket beneath the retained upper inner-leaf pier. It transfers that masonry and any superimposed facade/roof reactions into the end zone of the cross-beam; these loads and local flange/web resistance are NOT covered by a floor-only size assumption. Packing/grout product, compressive stress, restraint, thermal/fire detail and complete downward path require design.

elements.name: Basement · continuous RC raft trial
elements.section: 300 mm RC raft allowance; thickness and reinforcement NOT designed
elements.basis: Continuous reinforced-concrete raft concept under all six retaining-wall runs; no separate strip footings assumed beneath it. 300 mm is a spatial/budget allowance, not a thickness calculation. Local thickenings, punching, bending, crack control, wall-base fixity, waterstops, waterproofing and temporary works remain undesigned. The 352.5 mm retaining-wall envelope still coordinates the cavity wall above, not a calculated RC thickness. F02 lowers the raft top to -3.000 m beneath the unchanged -2.800 m finished floor, reserving 200 mm for the floor build-up. Retaining-wall and column bases follow the raft; excavation and groundwater heads update.

elements.name: Original garage rebuild · west footing
elements.section: 600 mm wide × 300 mm thick strip; underside 1.00 m below assumed ground
elements.basis: F01 reference: Characteristic/service-load budgets, not extracted reactions: garage reference 45 kN/m rounds a 24.6 kN/m two-storey masonry allowance (6 m x 0.205 m x 20 kN/m3), two floor allowances of 2.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m tributary width (12.5 kN/m), and roof 1.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m (3.75 kN/m). Garden 25 kN/m is a wall/terrace budget; 35 kN is an independent illustrative post reaction. Basement total superstructure 1,800 kN is a separate whole-footprint service budget, not a completed load takedown. Do not add the post budget to the line-load budget as if independently verified. G01: the illustrative superstructure budgets and additional permanent-load allowance exclude the separately measured vehicle deck, local RC bands/bearing nodes and cinema bearing masonry. Their actual modelled volumes and assumed densities are added explicitly. This is still not a load takedown; empty-box uplift excludes these later construction stages.
checks: Engineer to verify loading, capacity, stability and complete support path.

design.section: 250 mm RC slab spatial candidate; reinforcement and vehicle deck design unresolved

checks: Engineer to verify loading, capacity, stability and complete support path.
Coordinate bearings, connections, fire protection and installation tolerances before construction.

vehicleDeckStudy.status: Flexural equilibrium sensitivity only; reinforcement is NOT selected

vehicleBrief.ownerInstruction: Use conservative allowances: fully laden van up to 3.5 tonnes and Tesla up to 3.1 tonnes, potentially parked together.

assumptions.note: Axle fractions, track widths, wheel imbalance and movement factor are explicit study assumptions, not vehicle data or prescribed Eurocode values. The 30 kN jack case is a separate local floor action, not additional vehicle mass. Actual plated axle ratings and tyre/jack contact patches remain required.

codeBasis.provisionalCategory: G: both gross vehicle allowances exceed 30 kN
codeBasis.basis: Use first-generation EN 1991-1-1 with the applicable UK National Annex as the provisional project basis. JRC guidance gives Category G for 30-160 kN vehicles and a 5 kPa UDL. Exact UK concentrated-action requirements, combinations, access restrictions and edition must be confirmed by the designer. No 40-90 kN generic axle range is silently adopted as the selected UK axle load.

sources.title: JRC Eurocode 1 workshop, page 32
IStructE Eurocode transition guidance

limits: Two vehicles together is the operational brief, not a verified parking layout or full-deck load-pattern analysis.
UDL, axle pairs and local jack sensitivities are evaluated separately; the full vehicle weights are not added again to those actions.
Transverse spreading through topping/infill, tyre and jack patches, punching, beam torsion and joint transfer remain unverified.
The paired-wheel study assumes an axle parallel to the precast beam. Turning, wheelbase, both axles, edge approaches and loads shared through the central wall/opening heads need full layout analysis.
Vehicle weights are variable actions and must not be credited as permanent resistance to groundwater uplift.
No car lift, heavier vehicle or construction plant is included in this parking brief.

vehicleDeckStudy.supportSpanBasis: Wall-centre to wall-centre simply supported strips. No continuity/fixity credit. A local wheel/jack is placed at midspan; vehicle axle pattern and transverse load distribution remain unresolved.
vehicleDeckStudy.limits: No verified effective strip width, wheel/axle/jack positions, simultaneous actions, punching/one-way shear, cracking, long-term deflection, reinforcement continuity, anchorage, fire/exposure cover, bearing or construction-stage design. Required As is not an order or fixing schedule.

issues.title: Retained house: hidden structure unknown
issues.detail: Existing joists, rafters, foundations and steel are retained as grey architectural context, not invented as new members. New openings, stairs and added loads require targeted investigation.

issues.detail: Gallery joists now extend to the proposed west bearing line at X5.615 m, inside the roof overhang. The displayed steel receiver is an uncalculated space reservation. Its roof bearing seat, wall plate, rafter connection, glazing-head clearance and end supports are not detailed. Do not assume that the nearby rafter and beam meshes establish a buildable joint.

issues.title: Primary gallery and entrance beams: steel proposal, sizes unverified
issues.detail: The named gallery/eaves receivers and entrance-void beams are explicitly proposed in steel. Their UB profiles compare physical fit with the previous 300 mm timber reservations; no structural section selection is implied. Model segments sharing one beam-line reference do not specify fabrication splices. Beam joints, steel-compatible joist connections, bearings/padstones, deflection, roof/floor reactions, stability, fire protection and support to foundations remain to be designed.

issues.title: Full loft floor replacement is the agreed base scheme
issues.detail: Owner instruction 26 October 2026: remove the existing roof and loft joists entirely. Existing lower-storey structure remains unless altered. New-member dimensions, supports and temporary works require design. New joists cover the original-house, extension and gallery plates, excluding real openings. Roof B is the default. Reboarding alone is not a replacement structure; the new joists, bearings, bracing and construction sequence still need verification.

issues.title: Vault wall requires floor transfer and opening-head design
issues.detail: The omitted lower gable piers/head are restored. Two floor-level beam reservations show a possible support line for the brick and block leaves; no beam size is verified. The 1.2 m opening head is still uncalculated, and the shallow roof-scribed space at its jambs constrains a conventional lintel. Check bearings, wall loads, first-floor depth and foundations.

issues.title: Courtyard projection carried by an edge beam between wall piers
issues.detail: LP03: the accepted 720 mm architectural projection is carried by one continuous outer-edge beam over the first-floor north pier and retained original-house front pier. Gallery joists are simply supported between west and east receivers; the former under-joist bearing beam and free rim are retired. All support capacities, roof/facade eccentricity, restraint and connections remain unverified.

issues.title: Loft bearings: reuse existing solid walls; resolve local gaps
issues.detail: Owner identifies existing house walls as solid construction and proposes reusing them for loft-floor bearings. Candidate contacts follow actual retained wall geometry; wall material/strength, openings, wall-head seats and load path to foundations require survey and design. No blanket under-hip steel line is assumed. Missing contacts remain unresolved. The new west extension has no retained first-floor wall in this register and keeps its separate transfer reservation. Joists with no crossing wall remain flagged. Modelled wall heads can sit above the joist underside; no bearing pocket, wall reduction or hanger capacity is assumed. The west extension now has its own shorter east-west joist field; the old cross-room transfer is retired.

issues.title: Gallery notch closed; receiver and wall-head design remain open
issues.detail: Close only the small notch beside the former short steel return, to the west eaves bearing line X5.615. Preserve the larger entrance void south of Y-5.3 and the actual relocated stair opening. Retire the detached low-eaves floor-margin fragment outside this bearing line; it is not a separate joisted bay. No habitable headroom is claimed. The west eaves receiver extends to the main north transfer. M-FR-3-023/024 and their cantilever premise are retired. Existing wall bearing, masonry-head levels, the longer joist spans and the receiver/transfer connection still require design. No flange notches, bolts or welds are selected.

issues.title: New ground-floor joisted deck: basement transfer unresolved
issues.detail: The new wing, courtyard notch and entrance-link joists now follow their floor plates and preserve the basement stair opening. Their receiver network is a proposal. The long intermediate girder needs designed supports through the basement; retaining-wall bearings, moisture/fire details and deeper floor build-up remain unresolved. No existing house ground floor is replaced.

issues.title: Ridge and projection supports unresolved
issues.detail: Ridge/edge profiles are space reservations only, not selected beam sizes. The long ridge is not a verified single span. Intermediate supports, backspans, torsion, roof loads, splices, connections and a load path to ground are unresolved. B01 only has the limited UK-T01 screen.

issues.title: Stair trimming affects the tight headroom
issues.detail: Existing architectural check was about 2.01 m. New member depth/ceiling finishes can reduce this. Doubled members are reservations, not a completed stair trimming or connection design.

issues.title: Roof framing and terrace loading still require design
issues.detail: Rafters and perimeter members follow actual roof planes, rooflight cuts and dormer edges at a 400 mm layout. 45 × 220 and doubled edges reserve space only. Wind/snow, uplift, spans, hips/valleys, ridge joints, roof terrace loading, restraint, insulation and headroom not verified.

issues.title: Two roof strategies; both need structural verification
issues.detail: Option A retains and adapts the remaining original roof. Option B replaces it with a new frame to the same accepted exterior shape. Replacement framing is conditional on B and excluded from A quantities; common new wings/dormers remain in both. Demolition, weather protection, covering/insulation, surveys and local strengthening are not priced. The agreed complete loft-floor replacement is included independently. Existing lower-storey walls and floors remain except where altered.

issues.title: Wall assemblies need room / reveal coordination
issues.detail: New exterior leaf study uses 102.5 mm brick + 150 mm cavity + 100 mm block: 352.5 mm overall versus many 230 mm authored walls. Outer face retained; inner face can encroach by 122.5 mm. Orientation for ambiguous fragments is assumed. Dormer/knee-wall studwork and masonry junctions remain uncalculated; ties, plates, membranes and corners are not fully detailed.

issues.title: Opening heads are not a selected lintel schedule
issues.detail: Displayed head reservations are individually selectable, with 150 mm geometric end allowances. They are not manufactured Catnic sections. Check both leaves, load ratios, bearing capacity, floor/roof reactions, thermal details and compatibility. Wide heads may require steel rather than a cavity lintel.

issues.title: Internal framing roles are separated, not certified
issues.detail: Load-bearing role is proposed intent, not a capacity check. Explicit room partitions are proposed non-loadbearing; dormer external support frames and the gym bearing wall are structural proposals. Unassigned framing is separately marked for review; knee walls are not assumed non-loadbearing.

issues.title: Entrance link: concrete slab replaces floor joists
issues.detail: Owner instruction: concrete slab replaces the entrance-link joists between former receivers 18 and 17. 250 mm thickness is a space/quantity allowance, not a calculated slab. This area is outside the modelled basement; ground bearing is only a working assumption. Survey ground/backfill and resolve differential movement beside the basement. A suspended solution may be needed. Reinforcement, foundations, insulation, DPM/waterproofing, joints and support capacity remain unverified. A 10 mm joint envelope separates it from the adjoining basement concrete. The 100 mm floor-build-up allowance above it is not a selected screed/insulation specification. The structural slab must not be assumed to bridge unsupported backfill.

issues.title: Garden room / terrace frame added; capacities and roof depth unresolved
issues.detail: Steel receivers and six posts provide an explicit support proposal behind the glazing. Solid timber follows the three rooflight openings, with separate doubled side joists/headers. Sections, roof terrace loading/deflection, diaphragm stability, steel/wood connections, glazing tolerances and the projecting roof edge require design. The 225 mm architectural roof band is not a complete warm-roof/terrace build-up; resolve insulation, falls, waterproofing and finishes before fixing levels.

issues.title: Garden room poured slab and connected substructure included
issues.detail: The displayed garden slab is 150 mm thick, with 150 mm above it reserved to ground-floor FFL. The separate perimeter footing is 300 mm thick, with underside at model Z-1.15 m; that is 1.00 m below the assumed adjacent ground. Foundation masonry rises to the wall/post bases independently of the slab. These are the current F01 reference dimensions, not a surveyed founding depth or capacity approval. Ground, trees, fill, settlement, reinforcement, post bearings, damp protection and existing-house junctions remain unresolved.

issues.title: Garage over basement: vehicle deck and cinema bearing-wall proposal
issues.detail: Replace the vehicle-loaded garage/utility deck south of the basement stair with a suspended RC slab on the perimeter RC walls and strengthened cinema walls. Retain timber floor north of the cinema, on a shorter main steel girder. All dimensions are experimental; reinforcement, load spreading, foundations and connection designs remain unverified. Vehicle UDL and local wheel/jack actions must be designed separately from domestic floors. The 250 mm slab is NOT a verified reinforcement design; the one-way strip study exposes sensitivity to wheel-load distribution. The shorter northern UB passes its three explicit two-floor gravity budgets. Complete slab/wall/pad/raft design, groundwater effects, construction joints and temporary propping remain open.

issues.title: Short ground-floor bays: solid C24 and staggered blocking
issues.detail: Short northern suspended ground-floor bays use 45 × 295 mm solid C24 at 400 mm centres. This uses about 43% less net timber than the earlier 95 × 245 mm option; both are compared in G02. Garage vehicle bays remain the separate G01 concrete-deck concept. Same FFL, ceiling datum and support network; joists are 5 mm shallower than the earlier 300 mm I-joist reservation. Experimental floor-load candidate; no complete floor-system approval. Six load cases plus six smaller-section sensitivities are attached to each joist. Midspan blocking is drawn and a rough 4.8 m stock allocation reuses offcuts; vibration, restraint, fixings and services remain open.

issues.title: Reference footings and basement raft: assumptions only
issues.detail: F01 uses 600 × 300 mm strips at 1.00 m below assumed ground, foundation masonry above, a 150 mm garden floor slab and a 300 mm basement raft. Upper-case garage/garden-strip and house-post pressure and high-water basement uplift can exceed the chosen assumptions. Neither contact nor a passing gross-pressure comparison establishes adequacy: loads, settlement, eccentricity, trees/clay, adjacent foundations, reinforcement and temporary works must be resolved before excavation.

issues.title: Basement concrete is an envelope, not a reinforcement design
issues.detail: Model thicknesses and net volumes are shown. Reinforcement, ground-bearing/sliding/bending, water uplift, construction joints, underpinning, temporary retention and waterproofing are unresolved; no bar sizes or pour sequence inferred.

issues.title: Workshop steel and foundations unselected
issues.detail: Existing visual roof bars are shown for coordination. A real hollow/rolled section, connections, bracing, lintels and foundation scheme still need design; unselected steel is excluded from the priced subtotal.

issues.title: Repeated joists, transverse support and wide ground-floor opening
issues.detail: CJ01 repeated north/south main-wing joists. The garage/store bearing line continues through a wide steel head to the rear outside wall. A transverse loft girder preserves the open suite. Floor gravity candidates only; complete connections, support movement, masonry, roof/stability and foundations remain unverified.

issues.title: Seven-metre garage and flush wall junctions
issues.detail: CJ02: 7.0 m finished garage depth, independent nonbearing rear enclosure, straight entrance wall-face framing and a framed west-recess tail. Primary CJ01 supports and basement bearing walls remain. Revised gravity spans are screened; full design, wall/connection capacity, slab reinforcement and fire systems are unverified.

issues.title: Gallery cross-beam also replaces the junction opening head
issues.detail: The north gallery cross-beam and its west steel joint replace the overlapping generic lintel allowance. Complete opening-head and floor loads, joint design, bearing and distribution beyond the narrower steel flange remain unverified.

issues.title: One receiver at the gallery / north-east floor junction
issues.detail: LP03: the accepted 720 mm architectural projection is carried by one continuous outer-edge beam over the first-floor north pier and retained original-house front pier. Gallery joists are simply supported between west and east receivers; the former under-joist bearing beam and free rim are retired. All support capacities, roof/facade eccentricity, restraint and connections remain unverified.

issues.title: Gallery steel also supports upper masonry
issues.detail: The aligned cross-beam has an explicit top bearing bed below the upper block pier. Its design must include masonry, facade and any roof reactions as well as the floor. Complete reactions, restraint and beam/masonry capacity are not verified.

issues.title: Existing pier masonry within the floor zone is assumed
issues.detail: Grey retained-context bands show the assumed continuation between coincident existing piers. Material, condition, continuity and load capacity are unsurveyed; the bands are excluded from new-work quantities. New steel pockets and top bearing beds require design with all supported wall loads.

issues.title: Exterior masonry and gallery beam infill
issues.detail: Restore the exterior west-recess brick skin while retaining the internal stud tail; classify the first-floor courtyard window piers by their level and exterior role, not the historical Level loft label. Masonry support plates and fitted beam-channel infill are spatial proposals, not fabrication or capacity approval. Geometric masonry/plate/grout self-weight is added once to the linked floor-gravity screen, including the onward cross-beam reaction. These assumed densities are not selected product data. Beam torsion, shelf bending, welds, restraint, local flange/web effects, masonry strength, roof/facade actions, movement, fire/corrosion and thermal/moisture details remain unverified.

issues.title: Entrance returns and window jamb cavity closures
issues.detail: 50 mm-deep insulated vertical terminal and 3 mm moisture-resistant profile envelopes. Preserve the 150 mm cavity; no masonry bridge joins outer and inner leaves. UK supplier principle only, not a selected/tested assembly. Frame overlap, damp seals, cavity trays/weep drainage, fire performance, installation lengths/joints, restraint and thermal continuity require final detailing. Beam penetrations have a separate unselected compressible closure allowance; no fire rating is claimed.

issues.title: Masonry has separate concrete bearing; other wall transfers remain open
issues.detail: Continuous concrete bearing envelope under both cavity-wall leaves, independent of the room-side timber deck. Envelope only: RC thickness, reinforcement, anchorage, water/thermal separation, slab/foundation capacity and construction sequence are not designed. The six basement perimeter envelopes now connect through the floor depth to Z0. Timber ledgers sit beside them. The slab edge follows the corrected courtyard return. The wider floor-level masonry audit reports 33 leaves without complete geometric base contact; these require a wall continuation, lintel or designed transfer, never an assumed timber-header bearing.

issues.title: North/east wing masonry continues independently of the floor joists
issues.detail: Aligned north/east upper leaves continue through the 200 mm first-floor band onto corresponding masonry below. The missing corner return is restored. Floor ledgers and joists are set inside the blockwork face. Ledger anchors, masonry/lintel capacity, restraint and foundations are unverified; no load-bearing brickwork is assigned to timber joists. 0 measured wall/timber intersections remain in these corrected interfaces.

issues.title: Gallery deck and glazing edge coordinated to the bearing beam
issues.detail: 50 x 50 x 6 mm equal-angle spatial reservation against the outer edge of the west receiver top flange. Upper surface is flush with the deck underside. It supports the narrow remaining floor/glazing margin without changing glazing or habitable floor. Two pieces stop either side of the north facade masonry pier; no brick/steel notches are inferred. Flange-edge attachment, welds/brackets, beam torsion, facade self-weight/wind loads, fire/thermal separation, movement, waterproofing and fixings remain unverified. No product, fabrication weld or capacity approval is implied.

issues.title: Smaller beam proposal: compliance not demonstrated
issues.detail: UK gravity combinations retained. Two floor-only trials use a provisional 20 mm total movement target; wall/ground targets remain 10 mm. Movement compatibility, roof actions, stability, vibration, connections and supports remain unverified.

issues.title: Loft receiver load path: 0 members fail the linked floor screen
issues.detail: CJ01 repeated north/south main-wing joists. The garage/store bearing line continues through a wide steel head to the rear outside wall. A transverse loft girder preserves the open suite. Floor gravity candidates only; complete connections, support movement, masonry, roof/stability and foundations remain unverified.

issues.title: West loft: short-span solid timber replaces the unsupported transfer
issues.detail: Replace the unsupported cross-room transfer with an east-west solid-timber joist field over the shorter west-extension width. 89 x 235 mm C24 at 300 mm nominal centres is an experimental floor-only candidate, not an approved design. Perimeter timber receivers remain provisional wall-face ledgers and must bridge the window/door openings with designed anchors, heads, bearing and restraint. Roof reactions, heavy partitions, vibration, fire/acoustics and full wall/foundation load paths remain unverified.

issues.title: Aligned front-window wall bodies restored
issues.detail: The main architectural model already contains these wall bodies. Explicit structural mapping now includes their piers, sill walls and cavity-width lintel reservations. The first-floor band continues onto lower walls/heads, and reserved lintel pockets remove duplicate masonry volume. Lintel capacities, wall bearing, ties and damp/thermal details remain unverified.

issues.title: Extended eaves receiver: roof seats need design
issues.detail: The extended receiver intersects 12 rafter reservations. A coordinated wall plate/seat, restraint and roof/floor-level detail is still required. These small overlaps are retained and measured; no birdsmouth, rafter reduction or steel notch is approved simply to erase a clash.

issues.title: Authored floors, ceilings and roof linings: measured fit
issues.detail: 1159 overlaps remain in the expanded finish audit; 24 surfaces/member checks could not be measured. Horizontal floor framing is only one subset. Roof depth, bearing-pad finishes and remaining concrete interfaces require further architecture/structure coordination. See Connections & fit for exact authored covering names and member references.

issues.title: Beam ends: masonry pads, steel joints and unresolved supports
issues.detail: Horizontal rolled-steel beam ends only. Padstones are required where the bearing design calls for them; steel joints and direct reinforced-concrete supports are distinct. Geometric contact is not capacity verification. Non-profiled roof reservations and proprietary lintels require their own complete support design. 6 beams have at least one unresolved end in this geometric review.

issues.title: Junction detailing is still a proposal
issues.detail: Square-cut joist ends have nominal 3 mm end clearance beyond a 2 mm hanger back plate. Secondary beam ends and rafters are set back from steel faces; those gaps are modelling assumptions, not approved fabrication tolerances. Infill blocks reserve space only. Plates, bolts, welds, restraint, web stiffeners and bearing checks remain to be designed.

issues.title: Measured solid interferences remain
issues.detail: 81 positive-volume intersections remain in the audited member/wall systems. Some are intended bearing-pocket locations; others need a changed level, assembly or support. Inspect the Junctions view. Do not cut beam flanges or structural walls simply to remove a clash.

issues.title: Construction layers and floor depth require completion
issues.detail: Floor build-up envelopes are now individually selectable. The Junctions view lists unmodelled layers explicitly, including steel fire protection, wall ties/trays/barriers, roof membranes and basement waterproofing/reinforcement. These remain real omissions from the construction design.

issues.title: Non-bearing partition head clearances are provisional
issues.detail: Complete panel heads below parallel steel are lowered with their studs, retaining a continuous head plate. The 25 mm model gap reserves combined movement/fire-lining space only; actual structural movement, steel protection, lateral restraint and a compatible head/sealing system remain to be designed. Cross-beam junctions remain flagged.

roofOptions.externalForm: Both options keep the accepted external roof shape, dormers, levels and stair position. The choice concerns retaining versus replacing the existing roof structure.

options.label: A · Retain and adapt the existing roof
options.description: Keep surviving original-house roof structure where survey and load checks allow. Form the agreed dormers, roof junctions and new wings; allow for local strengthening and temporary support.
options.risks: Existing timber condition, connections, bearings and capacity are unverified. Local strengthening and the demolition already needed for the agreed alterations remain unpriced.

options.label: B · Remove and rebuild the existing roof
options.description: Strip the existing roof completely and construct the agreed roof shape with a new coordinated frame. New framing replaces every surviving original-roof surface shown in Option A; altered/new roof areas are common to both options.
options.risks: Requires a full replacement roof design, demolition/propping/weather protection, wall-head checks, temporary stability and connection design. Replacement member sizes currently reserve space only.

foundations.status: Experimental reference assumptions; not a site-average measurement or construction design
foundations.datum: Model ground-floor FFL 0.000 m; assume adjacent ground at -0.150 m solely for this study
foundations.boundsMeaning: Illustrative lower/reference/upper cases, not confidence bounds. Clay/tree effects, made ground, drains, groundwater or adjacent foundations can require deeper/wider foundations or a different system. Ashley Heights has mature trees: their influence is not assessed.

strip.stemMaterial: Foundation-grade masonry envelope; product and below-ground suitability unselected

gardenSlab.basis: Ground-bearing floor only. Perimeter walls and terrace posts bear on separate foundations. Reinforcement, subgrade, fill and insulation arrangement unselected.

basement.basis: Continuous reinforced-concrete raft concept under all six retaining-wall runs; no separate strip footings assumed beneath it. 300 mm is a spatial/budget allowance, not a thickness calculation. Local thickenings, punching, bending, crack control, wall-base fixity, waterstops, waterproofing and temporary works remain undesigned. The 352.5 mm retaining-wall envelope still coordinates the cavity wall above, not a calculated RC thickness. F02 lowers the raft top to -3.000 m beneath the unchanged -2.800 m finished floor, reserving 200 mm for the floor build-up. Retaining-wall and column bases follow the raft; excavation and groundwater heads update.
basement.floorBuildUpBasis: 200 mm dimensional budget above the raft, preserving the authored basement FFL. Waterproofing type, drainage/access, gas protection, insulation strength/thermal performance, screed reinforcement/drying and edge details are unselected. Layers must be redesigned with the waterproofing specialist and structural engineer; no system performance is claimed.

foundations.loadBasis: Characteristic/service-load budgets, not extracted reactions: garage reference 45 kN/m rounds a 24.6 kN/m two-storey masonry allowance (6 m x 0.205 m x 20 kN/m3), two floor allowances of 2.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m tributary width (12.5 kN/m), and roof 1.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m (3.75 kN/m). Garden 25 kN/m is a wall/terrace budget; 35 kN is an independent illustrative post reaction. Basement total superstructure 1,800 kN is a separate whole-footprint service budget, not a completed load takedown. Do not add the post budget to the line-load budget as if independently verified. G01: the illustrative superstructure budgets and additional permanent-load allowance exclude the separately measured vehicle deck, local RC bands/bearing nodes and cinema bearing masonry. Their actual modelled volumes and assumed densities are added explicitly. This is still not a load takedown; empty-box uplift excludes these later construction stages.
foundations.calculationBasis: Gross unfactored pressure screens against assumed gross allowable bearing, NOT Eurocode 7 ULS verification or settlement design. Include footing concrete 24 kN/m3, foundation masonry 20 kN/m3, soil cover on projections 18 kN/m3; raft/retaining concrete 25 kN/m3. Pressure screens omit eccentricity and local load spreading. Uplift uses water 9.81 kN/m3 at the raft underside and compares un-factored dead weight only, without relying on pumps or favourable soil friction.

layerSchedule.shown: 150 mm concrete slab, 150 mm finish/build-up zone, 150 mm sub-base allowance; perimeter foundations; terrace steel/timber and 22 mm deck with three rooflight apertures
layerSchedule.unresolved: Slab reinforcement and ground suitability; actual insulation/screed/DPM arrangement; roof terrace loading, falls, waterproofing, thermal layer and complete ceiling/roof depth. No pour or fabrication schedule.

layerSchedule.shown: 22 mm finish + 22 mm deck above members; coordinated flat ceiling datums with 31.5 mm lining and at least 25 mm service/suspension below the governing beam. G02 solid joists include staggered midspan blocking.
layerSchedule.unresolved: Selected deck/joints, acoustic infill, fire-rated lining assembly, vapour/air control, diaphragm restraint, hanger/ledger fixings and service routes remain unverified. Pitched/flat roof-lining conflicts are separate from the checked horizontal floor zones.

layerSchedule.shown: Basement FFL −2.800 m over 20 mm finish, 65 mm screed, 100 mm insulation and 15 mm waterproof/protection allowance above the raft. Garage spatial proposal: 22 mm finish + 53 mm screed over 250 mm RC.
layerSchedule.unresolved: Waterproofing system/joints, thermal/fire/acoustic assemblies, reinforcement, vehicle wheel/jack loading, slab deflection, wall-base starters through the 75 mm floor build-up and construction sequence require design.

layerSchedule.shown: Brick, 150 mm cavity space, blockwork, course pieces and lintel reservations
layerSchedule.unresolved: Insulation specification, drained cavity, ties, DPC, cavity trays, weep holes, cavity barriers, closers, movement joints and internal lining are not individually modelled.

layerSchedule.shown: Studs, plates, headers, rafters and fascia backing
layerSchedule.unresolved: Sheathing, bracing/straps, insulation, membranes, ventilation, battens, coverings, weathering and fire/acoustic layers are not fully detailed.

layerSchedule.shown: Real flange/web profiles, end-setback reservations, generic hangers and timber infill envelopes
layerSchedule.unresolved: End/fin plates, bolts, welds, stiffeners, anchors, padstones, shrinkage/movement and fire protection require design. No fabrication tolerances approved.

layerSchedule.shown: Concrete envelopes and new ground-floor framing
layerSchedule.unresolved: Reinforcement, joints/waterstops, waterproofing, drainage, insulation, gas/DPM layers, underpinning and temporary works are not designed.

junctionReview.scopeLimit: No clash-free or fabrication-ready certification. Existing hidden structure, MEP, fasteners, finishes and unmodelled layers remain outside the solid-intersection audit.

rateBasis: Editable owner-study GBP ex-VAT allowances, dated 26 October 2026. Not supplier quotes or a complete tender estimate. Low/high are sensitivity cases, not guaranteed bounds. Quantities are net model geometry; no waste or procurement rounding included.
excludedCosts: Retained structure (excluded, not valued at replacement cost)
Ground investigation, trial pits, design and statutory fees
Demolition, temporary works, propping and underpinning
Excavation, disposal, dewatering and ground remediation
Reinforcement, formwork, basement waterproofing and drainage

Decks, insulation, cavity ties/trays, DPCs, fire protection and finishes

garageOption.label: Original garage: demolition and rebuild — base scheme
garageOption.basis: Rebuild included by default. F01 uses 600 × 300 mm concrete strips, underside 1.00 m below assumed ground (model Z -0.15 m), with 850 mm foundation masonry rising to FFL 0. Soil and load values are explicit experimental assumptions; no surveyed site bounds or engineered depths. Ground investigation, tree effects, adjacent foundations, settlement and reinforcement remain unresolved.

loftFloor.scope: Full replacement of original loft joists and boarding; new joists across the complete loft footprint, with real stair/void openings preserved.
loftFloor.basis: Owner instruction 26 October 2026: remove the existing roof and loft joists entirely. Existing lower-storey structure remains unless altered. New-member dimensions, supports and temporary works require design.

groundDeckStudy.basis: Replace the vehicle-loaded garage/utility deck south of the basement stair with a suspended RC slab on the perimeter RC walls and strengthened cinema walls. Retain timber floor north of the cinema, on a shorter main steel girder. All dimensions are experimental; reinforcement, load spreading, foundations and connection designs remain unverified.

loads.limitations: VB01 owner vehicle brief. Use first-generation EN 1991-1-1 with the applicable UK National Annex as the provisional project basis. JRC guidance gives Category G for 30-160 kN vehicles and a 5 kPa UDL. Exact UK concentrated-action requirements, combinations, access restrictions and edition must be confirmed by the designer. No 40-90 kN generic axle range is silently adopted as the selected UK axle load. Two vehicles together is the operational brief, not a verified parking layout or full-deck load-pattern analysis. UDL, axle pairs and local jack sensitivities are evaluated separately; the full vehicle weights are not added again to those actions. Transverse spreading through topping/infill, tyre and jack patches, punching, beam torsion and joint transfer remain unverified. The paired-wheel study assumes an axle parallel to the precast beam. Turning, wheelbase, both axles, edge approaches and loads shared through the central wall/opening heads need full layout analysis. Vehicle weights are variable actions and must not be credited as permanent resistance to groundwater uplift. No car lift, heavier vehicle or construction plant is included in this parking brief.
loads.garagePartitionBasis: CJ02 95 mm nonbearing timber core with lined faces, 150 mm total allowance. 0.75/1.25/2 kN per metre bounds assumed self-weight including finishes; tested fire system not selected. Vehicle and wheel/jack ranges unchanged. Basement support axes unchanged.

stripStudy.limits: No verified effective strip width, wheel/axle/jack positions, simultaneous actions, punching/one-way shear, cracking, long-term deflection, reinforcement continuity, anchorage, fire/exposure cover, bearing or construction-stage design. solidFloorStudy.basis: Short northern suspended ground-floor bays use 45 × 295 mm solid C24 at 400 mm centres. This uses about 43% less net timber than the earlier 95 × 245 mm option; both are compared in G02. Garage vehicle bays remain the separate G01 concrete-deck concept. Same FFL, ceiling datum and support network; joists are 5 mm shallower than the earlier 300 mm I-joist reservation. Experimental floor-load candidate; no complete floor-system approval.
solidFloorStudy.loadBasis: Assumed superimposed floor Gk 0.75 / 1.00 / 1.35 kPa, including a lightweight-partition allowance, plus joist self-weight at 4.2 kN/m³. Alternative Qk 1.50 / 1.50 / 2.00 kPa or one 2.00 kN midspan point on a single joist. The point and distributed cases are separate sensitivities, not simultaneous. Heavy walls, vehicles and plant are excluded from these timber bays. These are assumptions, not certified statutory bounds.
solidFloorStudy.limits: Limited C24 bending, shear and deformation screen: Emean 11000 / Gmean 690 N/mm²; SC1; kdef 0.6; psi2 0.3; gammaM 1.3; kcr 0.67; kh=ksys=1. Instant <= min(L/300,8 mm), final <= min(L/250,10 mm) are study targets. Vibration, restraint, floor diaphragm, service penetrations, bearing and compatible hanger/ledger fixings, fire/acoustic/moisture assemblies and the onward load route remain unverified. No construction approval.

supplierReference.basis: UK supplier listing for 47 × 300 nominal / 45 × 295 finished C24; Davies page lists 4.8 m at £35.95 ex VAT. Listing is a supply benchmark, not a delivered quote or installed rate. Grade, moisture, durability, size/tolerance and availability require confirmation. The 44 × 293.5 mm case is an assumed smaller-section sensitivity, not a claimed supplier tolerance.

beamEndBearings.scope: Horizontal rolled-steel beam ends only. Padstones are required where the bearing design calls for them; steel joints and direct reinforced-concrete supports are distinct. Geometric contact is not capacity verification. Non-profiled roof reservations and proprietary lintels require their own complete support design.

galleryEdgeDetail.basis: 50 x 50 x 6 mm equal-angle spatial reservation against the outer edge of the west receiver top flange. Upper surface is flush with the deck underside. It supports the narrow remaining floor/glazing margin without changing glazing or habitable floor. Two pieces stop either side of the north facade masonry pier; no brick/steel notches are inferred. Flange-edge attachment, welds/brackets, beam torsion, facade self-weight/wind loads, fire/thermal separation, movement, waterproofing and fixings remain unverified. No product, fabrication weld or capacity approval is implied.

retainedPierNotches.basis: The real west retained pier and its upper wall occupy this corner; omit the exterior15mm sliver as well as actual masonry footprint.

galleryEdgeDetail.retainedContinuityBasis: The concealed 200 mm storey band is assumed to continue the existing solid pier where lower and upper architectural footprints coincide. Material, bond, condition and capacity require survey. A finite beam pocket and separate 10 mm top bearing bed preserve the upper wall; masonry/facade/roof reactions, local flange/web bearing, restraint, erection and temporary propping are not calculated. The grey band is retained context excluded from new masonry quantities.

beamOptimisation.status: Experimental smaller-section proposal; Building Regulations compliance not demonstrated
beamOptimisation.basis: UK first-generation Eurocode gravity combinations, 1.35 Gk + 1.50 Qk for the modelled adverse floor action; S355 grade with thickness-dependent yield strength. Member sizes remain preliminary. No safety factor has been reduced.
outstanding: Confirm actual permanent loads, partition positions, concentrated floor loads and every roof reaction; floor-only calculations do not verify roof support.
Check lateral-torsional stability and design compression-flange and end restraint, including construction stages.
Assess whole-floor vibration, deflection of flexible receiving supports and cumulative movement across connected beams and joists.
Agree movement limits and installation sequence with the ceiling, partition, glazing and floor-finish designs; 20 mm is an assumed coordination target, not a regulatory allowance.
Design steel joints, joist connections, web bearing/stiffeners, padstones and local masonry eccentricity and compression.
Verify the complete load path, wall stability, foundations, ground conditions and fire protection before construction.

elements.basis: Owner-selected beam-and-block system. The displayed 150 mm beams and 100 mm topping are provisional geometry, not accepted member sizes: vehicle/jacking load design, reinforcement, bearings and temporary works require supplier/engineer design. Solid RC is retained as a comparison; installed savings are not established.
checks: Current manufacturer design for beams, floor-grade infill, topping reinforcement and camber; no composite beam credit assumed.
Actual van gross/axle weights, paired wheel positions, jack contact patch, load distribution and local topping bending/punching; UDL and isolated point cases below are separate sensitivities.
RC edge strips, central closure and existing opening bands: reinforcement, anchorage, bearing stress, restraint and complete reactions through the masonry to the raft.
Basement lateral restraint/diaphragm and wall ties; water protection at edges, joints and garage threshold; groundwater uplift including construction stages.
Fire resistance from either side, protected basement ceiling, thermal insulation and acoustic layers. A legacy half-hour beam rating is not a complete garage/basement separation design.
Temporary erection stability, lifting access, wet topping and construction loads, cure period and propping. No cutting/drilling of prestressed beams.
Topping reinforcement, RC edge formwork, delivery/lifting, membrane/insulation, ceiling and professional design remain unpriced; quantities are not an order schedule.

vehicleBrief.ownerInstruction: Use conservative allowances: fully laden van up to 3.5 tonnes and Tesla up to 3.1 tonnes, potentially parked together.

assumptions.note: Axle fractions, track widths, wheel imbalance and movement factor are explicit study assumptions, not vehicle data or prescribed Eurocode values. The 30 kN jack case is a separate local floor action, not additional vehicle mass. Actual plated axle ratings and tyre/jack contact patches remain required.

codeBasis.provisionalCategory: G: both gross vehicle allowances exceed 30 kN
codeBasis.basis: Use first-generation EN 1991-1-1 with the applicable UK National Annex as the provisional project basis. JRC guidance gives Category G for 30-160 kN vehicles and a 5 kPa UDL. Exact UK concentrated-action requirements, combinations, access restrictions and edition must be confirmed by the designer. No 40-90 kN generic axle range is silently adopted as the selected UK axle load.

sources.title: JRC Eurocode 1 workshop, page 32
IStructE Eurocode transition guidance

limits: Two vehicles together is the operational brief, not a verified parking layout or full-deck load-pattern analysis.
UDL, axle pairs and local jack sensitivities are evaluated separately; the full vehicle weights are not added again to those actions.
Transverse spreading through topping/infill, tyre and jack patches, punching, beam torsion and joint transfer remain unverified.
The paired-wheel study assumes an axle parallel to the precast beam. Turning, wheelbase, both axles, edge approaches and loads shared through the central wall/opening heads need full layout analysis.
Vehicle weights are variable actions and must not be credited as permanent resistance to groundwater uplift.
No car lift, heavier vehicle or construction plant is included in this parking brief.

deeperBeamComparison.section: 125 × 225 mm at 530 mm centres — comparison only, not drawn
deeperBeamComparison.basis: A deeper beam is a credible supplier alternative, not ruled out: replace the 53 mm screed allowance with structural topping and lower the beam bearing datum by 22 mm. This requires revised wall seats and opening-head checks. Capacity, complete build-up and wheel sharing remain unverified; the shallower option is drawn solely to preserve all current interfaces.

foundations.status: Experimental reference assumptions; not a site-average measurement or construction design
foundations.datum: Model ground-floor FFL 0.000 m; assume adjacent ground at -0.150 m solely for this study
foundations.boundsMeaning: Illustrative lower/reference/upper cases, not confidence bounds. Clay/tree effects, made ground, drains, groundwater or adjacent foundations can require deeper/wider foundations or a different system. Ashley Heights has mature trees: their influence is not assessed.

strip.stemMaterial: Foundation-grade masonry envelope; product and below-ground suitability unselected

gardenSlab.basis: Ground-bearing floor only. Perimeter walls and terrace posts bear on separate foundations. Reinforcement, subgrade, fill and insulation arrangement unselected.

basement.basis: Continuous reinforced-concrete raft concept under all six retaining-wall runs; no separate strip footings assumed beneath it. 300 mm is a spatial/budget allowance, not a thickness calculation. Local thickenings, punching, bending, crack control, wall-base fixity, waterstops, waterproofing and temporary works remain undesigned. The 352.5 mm retaining-wall envelope still coordinates the cavity wall above, not a calculated RC thickness. F02 lowers the raft top to -3.000 m beneath the unchanged -2.800 m finished floor, reserving 200 mm for the floor build-up. Retaining-wall and column bases follow the raft; excavation and groundwater heads update.
basement.floorBuildUpBasis: 200 mm dimensional budget above the raft, preserving the authored basement FFL. Waterproofing type, drainage/access, gas protection, insulation strength/thermal performance, screed reinforcement/drying and edge details are unselected. Layers must be redesigned with the waterproofing specialist and structural engineer; no system performance is claimed.

foundations.loadBasis: Characteristic/service-load budgets, not extracted reactions: garage reference 45 kN/m rounds a 24.6 kN/m two-storey masonry allowance (6 m x 0.205 m x 20 kN/m3), two floor allowances of 2.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m tributary width (12.5 kN/m), and roof 1.5 kN/m2 x 2.5 m (3.75 kN/m). Garden 25 kN/m is a wall/terrace budget; 35 kN is an independent illustrative post reaction. Basement total superstructure 1,800 kN is a separate whole-footprint service budget, not a completed load takedown. Do not add the post budget to the line-load budget as if independently verified. G01: the illustrative superstructure budgets and additional permanent-load allowance exclude the separately measured vehicle deck, local RC bands/bearing nodes and cinema bearing masonry. Their actual modelled volumes and assumed densities are added explicitly. This is still not a load takedown; empty-box uplift excludes these later construction stages.
foundations.calculationBasis: Gross unfactored pressure screens against assumed gross allowable bearing, NOT Eurocode 7 ULS verification or settlement design. Include footing concrete 24 kN/m3, foundation masonry 20 kN/m3, soil cover on projections 18 kN/m3; raft/retaining concrete 25 kN/m3. Pressure screens omit eccentricity and local load spreading. Uplift uses water 9.81 kN/m3 at the raft underside and compares un-factored dead weight only, without relying on pumps or favourable soil friction.

LABC: raft foundation basics — reinforced raft, ground investigation and edge/internal stiffening
NHBC Standards 2024, chapters 4.3 and 5.4 — foundations and below-ground waterproofing guidance
NHBC Standards 2026 — warranty guidance distinct from Building Regulations

checksNotCompleted: Site investigation or a verified load takedown
Eurocode 7 ULS/SLS, settlement, eccentricity or local post/column bearing
Raft/wall flexure, shear, punching, crack control or reinforcement
Tree influence, ground heave, chemical class or drains
Waterproofing system, staged uplift, existing-house support or temporary excavation works

courtyardMasonryContinuation.basis: WM01 connected bearing geometry using F01 reference dimensions; not included in the garage/garden pressure checks. Ground, reinforcement, settlement and junction with deeper/retained foundations remain unverified.

foundations.garageDeckNote: BB01 changes only the garage deck self-weight in the existing unfactored pressure/uplift sensitivities. A lighter floor reduces pressure AND reduces uplift resistance. Empty-box construction stage is unchanged.

installation: Design supplier layout, bearings, topping/ties, local RC strips and temporary works together.
Construct verified basement walls and opening heads; check bearing levels and lifting access.
Install precast beams and floor-grade infill to supplier layout; no cutting or drilling of beams.
Grout joints, form remaining RC strips, install specified reinforcement/ties and membranes.
Place and cure designed topping with controlled construction loads; complete garage finish and protected/insulated basement ceiling.
